The [[1924 Summer Olympics]], officially known as the Games of the VIII Olympiad, was an international multi-sport event held in [[Paris]], France, from 4 May to 27 July. A total of 3,089 athletes from 44 nations participated in 126 events in 17 sports across 23 different disciplines.{{sfn|CNOF|1924|p=30}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/news/paris-1924-the-olympic-games-come-of-age |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240416012929/https://olympics.com/en/news/paris-1924-the-olympic-games-come-of-age |archive-date=16 April 2024 |access-date=12 July 2024 |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |title=Paris 1924: The Olympic Games come of age |url-status=live }}</ref>

Overall, athletes from 27 nations received at least one medal, and 19 of them won at least one gold medal. Athletes from the [[United States at the 1924 Summer Olympics|United States]] won the most medals overall, with 99, and the most gold medals, with 45.<ref name=still>{{cite web|url=https://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Paris-2024/2024-Factsheet-Paris-1900-and-1924.pdf [[Middle-distance running|Middle-distance]] and [[Long-distance running|long-distance runner]] [[Paavo Nurmi]] of Finland won the most gold medals for an individual at the Games and the most gold medals in athletics at a single Games, with five gold medals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/olympics-paris-1924-nurmi-gold-medals-paris-7b2083521bfbdc7470bc2045c326cb31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604023934/https://apnews.com/article/olympics-paris-1924-nurmi-gold-medals-paris-7b2083521bfbdc7470bc2045c326cb31 |archive-date=4 June 2024 |date=27 February 2024 |access-date=12 July 2024 |title=Paavo Nurmi's five Olympic running golds will be displayed in Paris next month |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=overview1924 /> Compatriot long-distance runner [[Ville Ritola]] won the most overall medals and the most medals in athletics at a single Games, winning six medals with four golds and two silvers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/paris-2024-summer-olympics/olympic-track-and-field-records-medal-count/3870535/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240628152548/https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/paris-2024-summer-olympics/olympic-track-and-field-records-medal-count/3870535/ |archive-date=28 June 2024 |access-date=12 July 2024 |date=28 June 2024 |publisher=[[WCAU|NBC10 Philadelphia]] |last1=Best |first1=James |title=Track and field Olympic records: Most medals, times to beat heading into Paris 2024 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=overview1924>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/8 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502015021/https://www.olympedia.org/editions/8 |archive-date=2 May 2024 |access-date=18 July 2024 |title=1924 Summer Olympics Overview |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Medal table==
[[File:Haiti Shooting Team – 1924 Summer Olympics.png|thumb|The [[Haiti at the 1924 Summer Olympics#Shooting|Haitian rifle team]] that won their nation's first medal of any color, a bronze in the [[Shooting at the 1924 Summer Olympics – Men's team free rifle|men's team free rifle event]]|alt=A group of five soldiers in front of a tent with a sign labeled "Haiti"]]
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC convention in its published medal tables. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation won, where a nation is an entity represented by a [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC). The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/186331923.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210801013923/https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/186331923.pdf |archive-date=1 August 2021 |via=[[CORE (research service)|CORE]] |last1=Sergeyev |first1=Yaroslav |title=The Olympic Medals Ranks, lexicographic ordering and numerical infinities |url-status=live}}</ref>

In [[Gymnastics at the 1924 Summer Olympics|gymnastics]], two silver medals (and no bronze) were awarded to [[Jean Gounot]] and [[François Gangloff]] for a second-place tie in the [[Gymnastics at the 1924 Summer Olympics – Men's sidehorse vault|men's sidehorse vault event]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.fr/jeux-olympiques/sochi-2014/2014/triples-francais-aux-jo-entre-le-saut-de-cheval-en-largeur-et-le-skicross-90-ans-d-attente_sto4144615/story.shtml |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240712075526/https://www.eurosport.fr/jeux-olympiques/sochi-2014/2014/triples-francais-aux-jo-entre-le-saut-de-cheval-en-largeur-et-le-skicross-90-ans-d-attente_sto4144615/story.shtml |archive-date=12 July 2024 |title=Triplés Français Aux Jo: Entre Le Saut De Cheval En Largeur Et Le Skicross, 90 Ans D'Attente|trans-title=French Trebles at the Olympics: Between the Sidehorse Vault and Skicross, 90 Years of Waiting |language=fr |access-date=12 July 2024 |date=20 February 2014 |publisher=[[Eurosport]] |url-status=live |last1=Dupuis |first1=Maxime }}</ref> while two bronze medals were awarded to [[Ladislav Vácha]] and [[August Güttinger]] for a third-place tie in the [[Gymnastics at the 1924 Summer Olympics – Men's rope climbing|men's rope climbing event]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1924/results/gymnastics-artistic/rope-climbing-men |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221204022047/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1924/results/gymnastics-artistic/rope-climbing-men |access-date=12 July 2024 |archive-date=4 December 2022 |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |title=Paris 1924 Gymnastics Artistic Rope Climbing Men Results |url-status=live }}</ref> In [[Rowing at the 1924 Summer Olympics|rowing]], no bronze medal was awarded in the [[Rowing at the 1924 Summer Olympics – Men's coxless pair|men's coxless pair event]], as there were only two teams that participated in the final after [[Gordon Killick]] and [[Thomas Southgate]] of [[Great Britain at the 1924 Summer Olympics|Great Britain]] got injured and did not start.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/157684 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240429215116/https://www.olympedia.org/results/157684 |archive-date=29 April 2024 |access-date=12 July 2024 |work=[[Olympedia]] |title=Coxless Pairs, Men |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Art competitions==
{{Hatnote|Note: [[Art competitions at the 1924 Summer Olympics#Medal_table]]}}
[[File:Hajos.jpg|thumb|Alfréd Hajós at the [[1896 Summer Olympics]], where he became the first Olympic champion in swimming before winning the silver medal at these Games|alt=A man in swimming attire holding an emblem inscribed with "Olympic Games" in Greek lettering and the numbers 776 and 1896 ]]
The 1924 Summer Olympics also included [[Art competitions at the 1924 Summer Olympics|art competitions]] across five disciplines: architecture, literature, music, painting, and sculpture, for works inspired by sport-related themes, were medal-eligible events at the time.<ref name=museum>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080501121223/http://www.olympic-museum.de/art/1924.htm |archive-date=1 May 2008 |last1=Wagner |first1=Jurgen |title=Olympic Art Competition 1924 Paris |url=http://www.olympic-museum.de/art/1924.htm |publisher=[[Olympic Museum]] |access-date=12 July 2024 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=music>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/920012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502071624/https://www.olympedia.org/results/920012 |access-date=12 July 2024 |archive-date=2 May 2024 |work=[[Olympedia]] |title=Music, Open |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Art competitions at the Summer Olympics|Art competitions]] were held from the [[1912 Summer Olympics]] until the [[1948 Summer Olympics]], but were discontinued over the [[Olympic Games#Amateurism and professionalism|amateurism controversy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/news/look-to-the-past-when-olympic-medals-were-awarded-for-architecture-music-and-lit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228075053/https://olympics.com/en/news/look-to-the-past-when-olympic-medals-were-awarded-for-architecture-music-and-lit |title=Look to the past: When Olympic medals were awarded for architecture, music and literature |archive-date=28 February 2023 |access-date=13 July 2024 |date=22 October 2021 |last1=Shestakova |first1=Indira |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |url-status=live}}</ref> Medals in art competitions are no longer recognized by the IOC as part of the total medal count.<ref name=smith>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111220142/http://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/When-the-Olympics-Gave-Out-Medals-for-Art-163705106.html |url=http://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/When-the-Olympics-Gave-Out-Medals-for-Art-163705106.html |url-status=dead |title=When the Olympics Gave Out Medals for Art |last1=Stromberg |first1=Joseph |work=[[Smithsonian (magazine)|Smithsonian]] |date=25 July 2012 |archive-date=11 November 2013 |access-date=12 July 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/02/us/paris-olympics-arts-medals.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240502104959/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/02/us/paris-olympics-arts-medals.html |title=They Used to Award Olympic Medals for Art? |date=2 May 2024 |archive-date=2 May 2024 |access-date=12 July 2024 |last1=Branch |first1=John |authorlink1=John Branch (journalist) |work=[[The New York Times]] |url-access=subscription |url-status=live}}</ref>

In architecture, no gold medal was awarded while the silver was awarded to the pair of [[Alfréd Hajós]] and [[Dezső Lauber]] of [[Hungary at the 1924 Summer Olympics|Hungary]]. Hajós became one of only two Olympians ever to have won medals in both sport (two golds in [[swimming at the 1896 Summer Olympics]]) and art Olympic competitions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/athletes/dezso-lauber |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703231945/https://olympics.com/en/athletes/dezso-lauber |archive-date=3 July 2022 |title=Dezső Lauber |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=12 July 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/news/hajos-turns-tragedy-into-glory-in-the-water |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230417210605/https://olympics.com/en/news/hajos-turns-tragedy-into-glory-in-the-water |archive-date=17 April 2023 |access-date=12 July 2024 |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |title=Hajos turns tragedy into glory in the water |url-status=live }}</ref> The bronze was awarded to [[Julien Médecin]] of [[Monaco at the 1924 Summer Olympics|Monaco]], who became the first Monégasque competitor to win an Olympic medal.{{efn|name=fn1|No longer recognized by the IOC as part of the total medal count<ref name=smith />}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://monaconow.com/le-comite-olympique-monegasque-incarnation-de-lolympisme-a-monaco/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231208213602/https://monaconow.com/le-comite-olympique-monegasque-incarnation-de-lolympisme-a-monaco/ |archive-date=8 December 2023 |access-date=12 July 2024 |title=The Monegasque Olympic Committee, the embodiment of the Olympic spirit in Monaco |work=Monaco Now |date=25 September 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In literature, one gold, which was awarded to [[Géo-Charles]] of France, two silvers to [[Josef Petersen]] of [[Denmark]] and [[Margaret Stuart (poet)|Margaret Stuart]] of Great Britain, and two bronzes to [[Charles Gonnet]] of France and [[Oliver Gogarty]] of [[Ireland at the 1924 Summer Olympics|Ireland]], were awarded.<ref name=museum /> Two compositions, entitled "The Land Where the Rose is Grown" and "O Vigila (now let the games begin)", that were part of the literature competition, were also part of the music competitions. The compositions were made by [[George Bamber]] of Great Britain, though no medals were awarded in the music competition as the jury could not reach a consensus to award medals for any of the competitors.<ref name=music />

In painting, [[Jean Jacoby]] of [[Luxembourg at the 1924 Summer Olympics|Luxembourg]] won the gold medal, becoming the first Luxembourgish competitor to win an Olympic gold medal,{{efn|This event is no longer recognized by the IOC as part of the total medal count.<ref name=smith /> Luxembourgish-born [[Michel Théato]] won the [[Athletics at the 1900 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon|men's marathon at the 1900 Summer Olympics]], but is credited as a French competitor without having applied for French citizenship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/fr/athletes/michel-theato |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220828115130/https://olympics.com/fr/athletes/michel-theato |archive-date=28 August 2022 |access-date=12 July 2024 |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] |title=Michel Théato |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=two>{{cite web|url=https://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/374.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502160249/https://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/374.pdf |archive-date=2 May 2024 |access-date=12 July 2024 |date=2018 |title=The Only Artist to Win Two Olympic Gold Medals |last1=Gricius |first1=Pierre |publisher=[[International Society of Olympic Historians]] |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Josy Barthel]] won the nation's first official gold medal, winning the [[Athletics at the 1952 Summer Olympics – Men's 1500 metres|men's 1500 metres event at the 1952 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/news/barthel-emerges-from-under-middle-distance-radar |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240422154602/https://olympics.com/en/news/barthel-emerges-from-under-middle-distance-radar |archive-date=22 April 2024 |access-date=12 July 2024 |title=Barthel emerges from under middle-distance radar |date=31 March 2021 |url-status=live |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] }}</ref>}} [[Jack Butler Yeats]] of Ireland won the silver, becoming the first Irish competitor to win an Olympic medal,{{efn|name=fn1}}<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/athletics/2024/04/13/the-story-of-how-jack-b-yeats-won-irelands-first-olympic-medal-in-painting/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240630182330/https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/athletics/2024/04/13/the-story-of-how-jack-b-yeats-won-irelands-first-olympic-medal-in-painting/ |archive-date=30 June 2024 |date=13 April 2024 |access-date=12 July 2024 |url-status=live |title=The story of how Jack B Yeats won Ireland's first Olympic medal ... in painting |newspaper=[[The Irish Times]] |last1=Clerkin |first1=Malachy |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and [[Johan van Hell]] of the [[Netherlands at the 1924 Summer Olympics|Netherlands]] won the bronze.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/920013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502071620/https://www.olympedia.org/results/920013 |archive-date=2 May 2024 |access-date=12 July 2024 |title=Painting, Open |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live }}</ref>

In sculpture, [[Konstantinos Dimitriadis]] of [[Greece at the 1924 Summer Olympics|Greece]] won the gold medal, [[Frantz Heldenstein]] of Luxembourg won the silver, and two bronze medals were awarded, one to [[Jean René Gauguin]] of Denmark and the other to [[Claude-Léon Mascaux]] of France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/201.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210830224644/https://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/201.pdf |archive-date=30 August 2021 |access-date=12 July 2024 |date=April 2010 |title=A Pair of Unknown Luxemburg Medalists and the Story of the Olympic Art Competitions |last1=Gricius |first1=Pierre |publisher=[[International Society of Olympic Historians]] |url-status=live }}</ref>
</onlyinclude>
